evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: The requested capability is clear and has a single reasonable interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: The action and object are specific enough to avoid materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website for info and updates
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “from the website” entails (UI form vs automated mailing), and what qualifies as “all the trainers” (role, current year, active trainers).

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: “Very clear map” is subjective and can be interpreted in materially different ways (interactive vs static, level of detail, accessibility).

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself ... and links to slides
evaluations.rationale: Unclear scope of “edit” (which fields/permissions) and unclear meaning of “and links to slides” (add links? manage attachments? required?).

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “per day” means (calendar day vs event day) and what counts as a “registration” (training vs summit vs camp registration).

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status ... if attendend, refunded, no show
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous set of statuses and definitions (e.g., “attended” vs “no show”), and “helps track” is underspecified.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous waitlist behavior (automatic promotion vs manual, ordering rules, notifications).

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “cancellation terms” are (where defined, which terms apply) and when/where the checkbox appears in the flow.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: “Whatever workflow exists” is unclear and allows multiple interpretations of where/how the deadline is enforced.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Conditional phrasing and undefined “my schedule” behavior makes the requirement materially interpretable in different ways.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: The requested information is specific (trainings the user registered for) with a clear intent.

evaluations.evidence: have a view ... that shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: “All attendee information” is ambiguous (which fields, privacy constraints), and the story mixes multiple intents without clear boundaries.

evaluations.evidence: all trainee information is shown and can be filtered
evaluations.rationale: “All trainee information” is ambiguous and could mean different data sets/fields; filtering behavior is not precisely defined.

evaluations.evidence: possibly a map view ... The following information must be shown
evaluations.rationale: “Possibly a map view” is ambiguous/optional without criteria; also “skill level” and “registrations remaining” may be interpreted differently without definitions.

evaluations.evidence: training options clearly marked ... level ... number of registrations, remaining registrations
evaluations.rationale: “Clearly marked” is subjective; “level” and registration counts can be interpreted differently (capacity vs current signups vs remaining seats).

evaluations.evidence: training landing page with an intro section ... and promote call for trainings
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “intro section” contains and what “promote call for trainings” means (banner, link, CTA, submission form).

evaluations.evidence: have a link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: A homepage link to a training list is a single clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Location and opening hours for a named place are clear and not materially open to interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous scope and rules for refunds (full vs partial, which sponsorship types, time limits, fees).

evaluations.evidence: link on the sponsorships page to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “become” entails (purchase flow, role assignment, confirmation) and what exactly the link targets.

evaluations.evidence: attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: “Associated with this company” is ambiguous (self-declared employer, sponsorship purchaser, domain match, admin-assigned).

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “identify myself as” means (select company, create company profile, verify affiliation) and resulting system state.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: “Maintain” is ambiguous (edit fields, archive, delete, manage rooms?) and venue attributes are unspecified.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details ... see the events happening there
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what constitutes “venue details” and what “events happening there” includes (sessions, trainings, summits; time window).

evaluations.evidence: sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous association rule (sessions they present? attend? registered for?) leading to materially different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “registration process” refers to (camp vs sponsorship vs training) and what the payment page must contain/handle.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous assignment semantics (levels, ordering, multiple sponsors, display rules) and what qualifies as “events”.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: Given the domain terms used elsewhere, the request is clear: list items sponsored by a sponsor.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged for an individual sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “individual sponsorship” options exist and charging rules (amount selection, confirmation, retries).

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: “Link attendees” is ambiguous (associate attendee profiles to sponsor? display list? manual vs automatic linkage).

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Editing one’s own profile is a standard, single-meaning requirement in this context.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup is a clear, commonly understood action with no materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “for consumption by Drupal Planet” requires (specific taxonomy term, metadata, feed inclusion rules).

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is a clear capability with a single primary interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading blog content is clear and not materially open to interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit that matches my brand
evaluations.rationale: “Matches my brand” is subjective and can lead to different functional interpretations (filtering, recommendations, categories).

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Summit registration is a clear action with a single intent.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: “Detailed directions” is vague (map vs step-by-step, transit modes, starting point) allowing materially different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Listing the user’s registered summits is clear and specific.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: The requested list is clearly defined by summit registration.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: “Basic information” is ambiguous (which fields are included) and can be interpreted in materially different ways.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “sponsors” includes (levels, in-kind, ordering, logos vs names) and display rules.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: “Agenda” is underspecified (sessions vs time blocks, speakers, locations, formatting) leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous definition of “seats left” (capacity minus registrations? confirmed payments? holds/waitlist).

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: “Specific details” is vague and can refer to many different information sets and page behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: A list of all summits is a clear, single-meaning requirement.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: The intent to view information describing sponsorship levels is clear in this domain.

evaluations.evidence: WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what counts as “long-form content” and which content types/fields are included.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Adding a link from job listings to a sponsorship profile is clear and not materially open to interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous who/what “the sponsorship person” is (role, specific contact) and what “learn about” must include.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous job posting workflow and constraints (approval, required fields, duration, eligibility as sponsor).

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the job board is a clear capability with a single interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous relationship between room and location (room already implies location) and what constitutes a “time slot” (session length, schedule grid).

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: A schedule view is a clear, commonly understood feature in an event context.

evaluations.evidence: final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “final” means (after what cutoff) and what qualifies as “approved” (accepted vs scheduled).

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Bulk-changing session status to accepted is clear in intent; details of UI are not required to avoid ambiguity here.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Setting a session’s status to accepted is a single clear action.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “evaluated” means (scored, accepted/rejected, reviewed) and notification channel/timing.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous notification channel and what constitutes successful submission (draft vs final).

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing one’s own submitted session is clear and not materially open to interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp, so that I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether this is speaker account registration, session submission, or both; “register to speak” can mean different workflows.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session for evaluation is a clear action in this context.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: “Personalize” is ambiguous (what elements can be changed: logo, text, colors, layout, links) leading to different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “when they are” requires (date only vs date+time, timezone, duration).

evaluations.evidence: offered several choices of idividual sponsorship on the second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what “registration” refers to and what “several choices” are (which options, pricing, selection rules).

evaluations.evidence: easily find a link in the menu
evaluations.rationale: “Easily find” is subjective and can be interpreted in materially different ways (placement, labeling, prominence).

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: User account registration via a form is clear and has a single primary interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: “Session information” is ambiguous (which fields, which sessions, search vs browse) allowing materially different requirements interpretations.
